scenario: AITA for telling someone disabled they should leave the gym | Throwaway for the usual reasons I go to the gym a few times a week as it's something I enjoy. Yesterday I was there for the first time this year and there was lots of new people which is to be expected this time of year with people making resolutions they can't stick to. Anyway I was minding my own business when I looked up and saw an overweight woman come in who had a walking stick, she also had who turned out to be her husband with her who looked like a gym regular. I saw her get on the exercise bike for about 20 minutes then she moved to the weight machines. Because of her disability she couldn't manage on and off the machines herself and her husband was helping her on and off between his workout. I was concerned about this and no staff were about so I went upto her and told her I think it's for the best she leaves the gym as she's clearly not able bodied enough for it (looking back now I should have worded it better). Her husband then came up and asked if everything was ok and I told him my concerns. He raised his voice slightly at me and told me to mind my own business as he's qualified in training different sports and she was in safe hands. I then told them I don't think the gym management would be too happy at someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. He told me his wife wasn't actually allowed to join the gym without a Dr's letter and also a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a plan for her to safety evacuate the building with the help of staff and all staff were aware of her problems. At this point I realised they weren't going to leave so went back to my workout. Today I told my friend what happened and he told me I'm an idiot who should learn to mind his own business or try encourage someone who's new to the gym. He doesn't attend the gym so I don't feel he understands the kind of environment she was in. He also seems to think my membership could be at risk for what I said

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me start by understanding the situation. The person in question is a Muslim who went to the gym and saw an overweight woman with a walking stick. Her husband, who seems to be a regular gym-goer, was helping her on and off the machines. The person was concerned because the woman couldn't manage the machines herself, and there was no staff around. So, they approached her and told her they think she should leave the gym because she's not "able-bodied enough." Later, her husband confronted them, explained that he's qualified and that the gym management is aware of her situation, including a doctor's letter and a safety evacuation plan. The person then realized they weren't going to leave and went back to their workout. They later told a friend, who called them an idiot and suggested they should mind their own business or encourage her instead. Now, I need to evaluate if the action taken by the person was morally acceptable. Let's break it down. First, the person's intention was to ensure the woman's safety. They noticed she couldn't manage the machines and there was no staff, so they approached her out of concern. That's a good intention. However, the way they approached her was problematic. Telling someone they should leave the gym because they're not "able-bodied enough" is disrespectful and could be seen as discriminatory. It's important to consider how such comments might make someone feel, especially someone who might already be vulnerable due to their disability. Additionally, the person made assumptions about the gym management's policies and the woman's ability to be there. They didn't know that the woman had a doctor's letter and a safety plan in place. Making such assumptions without knowing the full context can be harmful. The person's friend's reaction also indicates that their approach was not appropriate. The friend suggested they should mind their own business or encourage her instead, which aligns with the idea that interfering in this way was not the best course of action. In Islam, there are teachings about respecting others, maintaining good character, and not causing harm. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized the importance of kindness and avoiding harm. In this case, the person's actions, while well-intentioned, led to harm by making the woman and her husband feel judged and possibly uncomfortable. Moreover, in many Islamic teachings, it's encouraged to help others in a kind and respectful manner, not to judge or interfere without proper knowledge or invitation. Encouraging someone or offering help in a supportive way would be more in line with these teachings. So, considering all this, the action taken was not morally acceptable because it involved disrespectful and potentially harmful behavior, even if the intention was to help. The person should have approached the situation differently, perhaps by offering assistance or speaking to the gym staff instead of directly telling the woman to leave.
